One of my favourite games -- wrestling for a top-10 spot right now. An absolute love-letter to a bygone era of collectathons and a brilliant amalgamation of their unique highlights, lovingly-crafted as a tribute to each in a small way, pulled together into a cohesive ball of creativity and solid kinetic feel-good motion.

And then you unlock Death Wish, and prepare for the most grueling, sadistically crafted challenge in any 3D platformer. And I love it to death... wish. I've got a soft-spot the size of Isle Delfino for Master Quest style hard modes in games, and Death Wish delivers like the best of them. Remixed missions and challenges and bosses coming off the already wonderfully creative world just means a new, more focused angle to appreciate it all from, assuming this brand of self-inflicted torture is your kind of thing. Just remember that the tools the game offers for you are all intended ways to play. No shame in taking the Peace and Tranquility route just to unlock stuff, even though you might, like me, consider it a matter of personal accomplishment to not have.

Add onto all this the extreme level of mod support -- including a few that I would consider essential from go for a more solid experience (Diary+ and Death Wish Ultimate especially) -- and good-natured cutting humour, and you've got yourself one of the most fun, charming, and addictive games in the genre. A Masterpiece that is set to be a modern classic! The more you play, the more you get into it.

The good:
- The settings are variegated, rich of content and never boring.
- The characters are very well written and the voice acting is superb!
- The dialogues and writing in general are solid and actually funny.
- The protagonist is cute and versatile.
- Controls are extremely smooth and fluid.
- The difficulty is optimal for fun and has challenge. Nothing is really all that easy, and there are more difficult sections, so there's definitely satisfaction in completing levels.
- I never found serious bugs. Just rare, minimal glitches.

The bad:
- Some visual stuttering but fortunately only while loading levels. While playing, there's no problem at all.

Little note: Every time I replay the game, the first 10 minutes feel a little clunky. I played and replayed the game numerous times and I still haven't get what's the problem. After that, everything is wonderfully polished and amazing.

Vote: 9.5/10

A Hat In Time is a fun 3D platformer with a lot of charm. It has a nice mix of levels that are specific segments for that one time piece, an area getting used for multiple pieces (like Super Mario 64), and some wider free roam areas. It's not a very long game to complete but it spends its runtime well and has a challenge levels if you want them (even more so with the Seal the Deal DLC). The DLC are nice additions as well and are worth picking up. If you are looking for more to do the Steam Workshop integration makes getting more levels easy to do. I didn't try the co-op, but I'd imagine it would be a fun mess.

One of my absolute favourite games ever made. A Hat in Time is like a relaxing vacation from your everyday games, focusing more on raw fun, exploration and silliness, rather than anything competitive.

The graphics are extremely beautiful. I found myself using the camera function to take pictures of the landscape very often.
The main character is very cute (very important).
Controls are easy to learn.
Dialogue, characters and cutscenes are funny and cute.
There is no shortage of levels and worlds to explore. The worlds themselves are very different from eachother.
There are quite a lot of abilities you can unlock and/or buy.

A must-buy for every platformer lover.

Over the years I've tried to enjoy the game but every single time when I play I get reminded why I have started to dislike it so much. The game's physics, camera and controls are frustrating to try and play with, no matter if you happen to have a controller or use the keyboard and mouse. The camera flickers too much even with the lowest possible camera movements or doesn't follow in time. Lots of sequence breaks or automatic sequences that messes you up and the bright all time bloom effect does not make the game Epileptic friendly.

Kickstarter. 3D platformer. A team woth low to no experience. This had all in to be a flop, but it wasn't. Instead, it's one of the more well constructed, beautiful, fun and overall one of the best experiences from 2018, if not the best. The voice actors do an amazing job, the music is fantastic, the humour is exceptional, the gameplay is tight and just good, the visuals have a hint of the gamecube era and more. For any 3D platformer intusiastic, for anyone looking for a cute nice game to play, for anyone looking for a challenge, for any game enthusiast and anyone who's trying to look at good game design woth examples, this game is perfect for you. I can't stress enough how this game is beautifully constructed and played. An amazing job gears for breakfeast, I'll be looking forwards to your next game. Sincerely, a fan.
